posts.text: Releasing Muse Ember today -- our smallest model that delivers higher intelligence per dollar than others in its class. Built for token-heavy work that agents repeat all day: tool calls, coding subtasks, routing, extraction, and long document parsing. Available today on the Meta Model API and in Muse Code.
posts.why_viral: CEO-level announcement of Meta's efficient small model optimized for agent workloads.
posts.why_it_matters: Cost-efficient model for high-volume agent tasks like tool use and coding, available via Meta's API.

posts.text:
Meet Gemini 4 Hydrogen.

It brings cutting-edge intelligence to everyone, with speed and efficiency for everyday coding and agentic work.

Across 4 thinking levels, it stands on its own or teams up with Carbon and Argon — 2.5X faster than 3.8 Flash, outpacing competing models in its class.
posts.why_viral: Official Google launch of a fast, efficient Gemini model for coding and agents.
posts.why_it_matters: New speed/efficiency options for agentic coding with multiple thinking levels and multi-model orchestration.

posts.text: When Anthropic release a new model it's always worth taking a look at their updated prompting guide - here's an entertaining tip to make Fable 5.2 less likely to be cautious in how it improves existing code: tell it "This codebase is yours" https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/prompt-engineering/prompting-claude-fable-5-2#say-who-owns-the-code
posts.why_viral: Concrete prompting tip from a respected developer that improves model behavior on codebases.
posts.why_it_matters: Simple ownership framing reduces over-caution when models edit existing code.

posts.text: I've recently started hiding the bulk of my AI-generated GitHub PR descriptions behind a collapsed <details><summary> HTML tag (thankfully supported by GitHub Markdown) and I think it's a useful pattern for making PR slop a little bit less exhausting https://simonwillison.net/2026/Nov/9/details-summary/
